_meta.notes: DRAFT — NOT WIRED. Texas statewide elected executives. Every press listing below was fetched live on 2026-07-25 with a hardened httpx client (browser-class headers, see pipeline/lib/http.py); none of the seven is behind a WAF at the listing level and none needs Playwright to enumerate items. The single exception is texasagriculture.gov, whose ARTICLE DETAIL pages (not the listing) serve a bot-challenge to httpx and to the Internet Archive crawler; a real browser clears it, so that one row is marked requires_js on the detail leg only. Do not register this file in pipeline/lib/seeds.py until the two open scope questions in open_questions are answered. Texas also elects its Supreme Court, Court of Criminal Appeals and State Board of Education; those are out of scope here. The Secretary of State is appointed by the Governor, not elected, and is excluded for that reason.
open_questions: Railroad Commission attribution: three separately elected commissioners share one institutional /news feed. Some release titles name a commissioner ('Wayne Christian Backs Effort to Lower Government Cost'), most do not ('Texas Oil and Gas Production Statistics for April 2026'). Decide whether to store one agency-level official or three per-commissioner officials with a title-match attribution rule before wiring.

GLO scope: the /about-glo/press-releases feed mixes Land Commissioner output with Veterans Land Board operational notices ('Voices of Veterans', unaccompanied-veteran burial announcements). Roughly half the 2026 items are agency-programmatic rather than commissioner-attributable. Decide whether to collect all of it or filter.

members.notes: The only Texas executive needing a browser. Listing enumeration works fine over plain httpx — titles, URLs and sequential article IDs all extract — but published_at and body_text require rendering the detail page. Article IDs are NOT a usable date proxy: the same /Article/{id}/ space contains non-news site content (for example /Article/1061/awep, /Article/1297/brand-registration), so ID arithmetic across the news listing is meaningless. Sid Miller's output is unusually newsworthy right now (New World screwworm, data-center moratorium, public disputes with the Governor), so this row is worth the browser cost.
